issues.description: The UML in the problem statement specifies Stock.add(String) as returning void, but both the template and the solution implement Stock.add(String) to return an int (the new quantity or -1). This mismatch between the documented return type and the actual method signature can confuse students about the expected behavior and signature to use when interacting with Stock.add.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the problem statement UML with the code: update the UML to declare +add(String): int and document the return values (new quantity or -1) so students know the actual method signature and expected behavior. Alternatively, if the intended design is void, change the template and solution method signatures and implementations to void (and adapt usages), but updating the UML is the less disruptive fix.
